newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BSE bourse extends market suspensions.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BSE bourse extends market suspensions.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) decided to extend the suspension of its traditional, or non-standardised futures and options markets for an indefinite period as the markets are not sufficiently regulated, the BSE said on Wednesday.

"The BSE Council found that the markets cannot be operated any longer within current regulations and safety framework, and decided to uphold the suspension for an indefinite time," the BSE said in a statement in its official gazette.
The Council decided on the suspension from November 8 to December 3 some two weeks ago as certain deals had showed that security of trading on these markets was inappropriate, the BSE said.
The decision did not affect the BSE's standardised futures market. The BSE does not yet have a standardised options market.
The BSE also discovered some two weeks ago that a bourse member, Csiky Securities Kft, had been in an option deal involving unusually high risks.
Csiky was suspended by the BSE for indefinite time, saying information published by the brokerage had not given a clear picture of risks involved in its activities.
The bourse said on Wednesday that it planned to work out regulations for the non-standardised options market "within a relatively short period."
Bourse officials were not available for comment.
The Council also decided that the BSE should introduce strong measures to develop the standardised futures market so as to enable it to replace non-standardised trading, the statement said.
